$comment: Mtek CPU/GPU numeric tolerances (spec/testing.md section 5; task M2-08; decision 0043).
One entry per Mtek operation of the CPU conformance table cpu.json (key: callee, then the argument class
'(float)'/'(integer)' or a concrete signature). 'wgsl' is the WGSL the shader lowering emits for it (decision
0041); 'compare' is 'exact' (bit for bit, except where a quoted WGSL rule permits a difference: zero sign,
flush to zero, the other neighbour of an inexact integer-to-float conversion) or 'tolerance' (the GPU value
must lie in the interval WGSL allows for the exact inputs, widened by cpuRoundingUlp at each end).
'accuracy' is the machine form of the f32 bound transcribed from W3C WGSL [S5] section 15.7.4.1; 'cite' quotes
the spec text verbatim (superscripts of the HTML written as ^, e.g. 2^-126), each with its section number and
anchor (https://www.w3.org/TR/WGSL/#<anchor>). Inherited bounds are evaluated with interval arithmetic over the
quoted WGSL expression (tests/browser/support/numeric-accuracy.ts), every sub-operation with its own entry and
the global rules below (rounding up or down, reassociation, fusion, flush to zero, overflow).
'domain' lists the input domain; inputs outside the domain or outside the range an accuracy statement is given
for are not compared (WGSL: 'the accuracy is undefined for input values outside that range') and are listed in
gpu-not-compared.json. Never widen an entry to make a test pass (blueprint section 14): a disagreement is a
lowering bug or a spec issue with a decision record.

rules.quote: The correctly rounded result of the operation for floating point type T is: x, when x is in T, Otherwise: the smallest value in T greater than x, or the largest value in T less than x. That is, the result may be rounded up or down: WGSL does not specify a rounding mode.
rules.use: A correctly rounded sub-operation contributes the interval [round down, round up] of its exact result. Mtek still requires bit-exact + - * on hardware (spec/testing.md section 5): that is a Mtek promise stronger than WGSL (decision 0043).

rules.quote: If x is in the finite range of the floating point type, then ULP(x) is the minimum distance between two non-equal, finite floating point numbers a and b such that a ≤ x ≤ b (i.e. ulp(x) = mina,b|b - a|). Otherwise, ULP(x) is |b - a| where b and a are the largest and second-largest representable finite floating point values.
rules.use: ulpF32 in tests/browser/support/numeric-values.ts; an n-ULP bound widens the exact result x to [x - n ULP(x), x + n ULP(x)].

rules.quote: An expression that the accuracy is inherited from. That is, the accuracy of the operation is defined as the accuracy of evaluating the given WGSL expression. The given expression is only one valid implementation of the function. When evaluating the inherited-from expression, subexpression evaluations are subject to other rules for floating-point evaluation, including those regarding rounding, overflow, reassociation, fusion, and flush-to-zero.
rules.use: kind 'inherited': the expression is evaluated with interval arithmetic, each operation by its own entry.

rules.quote: When the accuracy for an operation is specified over an input range, the accuracy is undefined for input values outside that range.
rules.use: Rows whose inputs (or the inputs of an inherited sub-operation) leave the stated range are not compared; they are listed in gpu-not-compared.json and their GPU values are reported informationally.

A chain of three or more + and - terms is bounded as an exact sum plus one rounding of at most ULP(sum of the term magnitudes) per addition, whatever the order; likewise a chain of three or more products.

rules.quote: An implementation may fuse operations if the transformed expression is at least as accurate as the original formulation.
rules.use: Covered by the intervals: an unrounded product lies inside the interval of the rounded one.

rules.quote: Any inputs or outputs of operations listed in § 15.7.4 Floating Point Accuracy may be flushed to zero. Additionally, intermediate result values of operations listed in § 17.2 Bit Reinterpretation Built-in Functions, § 17.9 Data Packing Built-in Functions, or § 17.10 Data Unpacking Built-in Functions may be flushed to zero. Other operations are required to preserve subnormal numbers.
rules.use: An interval that reaches a subnormal value also contains 0. An exact row with a subnormal input or result accepts the flushed value (reported separately). Constructors and bit reinterpretations of i32/u32 must preserve subnormals.

rules.quote: Implementations may ignore the sign field of a floating point zero value. That is, a zero with a positive sign may behave like a zero a with a negative sign, and vice versa.
rules.use: An exact row whose result is a zero accepts a zero of either sign (reported separately).

rules.quote: Implementations may assume that overflow, infinities, and NaNs are not present during shader execution. In such an implementation, if the intermediate result of evaluating a runtime expression overflows, or yields an infinity or a NaN, the final result will be an indeterminate value of the target type.
rules.use: Rows with non-finite inputs or results are non-portable in cpu.json; an interval that may overflow (any intermediate beyond the finite range) is not compared.

If T is a floating point type, the result is equal to: e1 - e2 * trunc(e1 / e2).

entries.note: The 2.5 ULP of x / y can move trunc(x / y) to the neighbouring integer when x / y is within 2.5 ULP of an integer; the interval then spans both remainders, as WGSL allows.

If T is a signed integer scalar type, evaluates to: If e2 is zero: […] Otherwise, e1. If e1 is most negative value in T, and e2 is -1: […] Otherwise, e1. truncate(x) otherwise, where x is the real-valued quotient e1 ÷ e2.
If T is an unsigned integer scalar type, evaluates to: If e2 is zero: […] Otherwise, e1. Otherwise, the integer q such that e1 = q × e2 + r, where 0 ≤ r < e2.

If T is a signed integer scalar type, evaluates e1 and e2 once, and evaluates to: if e2 is zero: […] Otherwise, 0. If e1 is the most negative value in T, and e2 is -1: […] Otherwise, 0. Otherwise, e1 - truncate(e1 ÷ e2) × e2 where the quotient is computed as a real value.
If T is an unsigned integer scalar type, evaluates to: if e2 is zero: […] Otherwise, 0. Otherwise, the integer r such that e1 = q × e2 + r, where q is an integer and 0 ≤ r < e2.
-e: T | Negation. Component-wise when T is a vector. If T is an integer scalar type and e evaluates to the largest negative value, then the result is e.
If X is exactly representable in the destination type T, then XOut is the value in T equal to X. Additionally, if X is zero and of integer scalar type, then XOut has a zero sign bit.

If X lies between two adjacent finite values in T, then XOut is one of those two values. WGSL does not specify whether the higher or lower representable value is chosen, and different instances of such a conversion may choose differently.

entries.note: Bit-exact when the integer is representable; otherwise either neighbour is accepted (spec/language.md section 6.5), the other neighbour reported separately.

cite.quote: If X is a NaN, the result is an indeterminate value in T. If X is exactly representable in the target type T, then the result is that value. Otherwise, the result is the value in T closest to truncate(X) and also exactly representable in the original floating point type.
1e20f converted to i32 is the maximum i32 value, 2147483520i Note this is smaller than the maximum i32 value 2147483647i

entries.note: The WGSL result of an out-of-range input is the clamp to [-2^31, 2147483520], not to the i32 maximum; the CPU clamps to 2147483647 (decision 0037 item 6). Decision 0043 records the disagreement.

cite.quote: If X is a NaN, the result is an indeterminate value in T. If X is exactly representable in the target type T, then the result is that value. Otherwise, the result is the value in T closest to truncate(X) and also exactly representable in the original floating point type.
1e20f converted to u32 is the largest float value representable in u32, 4294967040u Note this is smaller than the maximum u32 value 4294967295u

entries.note: As for i32: WGSL clamps to 4294967040, the CPU to 4294967295 (decision 0043).

The domain is all vectors except the zero vector.

entries.note: Lowered to the generated helpers mtek_normalize_*: x / sqrt(x.x*x.x + x.y*x.y + ...) summed left to right, the zero vector when that length is 0 (decision 0047). The exactRows are the zero, underflowing and overflowing vectors, outside the WGSL domain, where CPU and GPU agree bit for bit; the other rows stay within the tolerance because the GPU divider is not correctly rounded.
